messages:
sam: Customer on enterprise VPN sees intermittent 502s from our hosted API. They say there is no request id in the response headers, and they can't upload a HAR. Asking how to collect a minimal repro we can escalate.

maria: Short checklist to send them (non-technical first):
- exact endpoint + path used (full URL) and approximate timestamps (UTC)
- the HTTP method and body (or a screenshot)
- a screenshot of Network tab -> select request -> Headers (Response headers area)
- if they can, Copy -> Copy as cURL and paste (redact auth token)

sam: they said corp proxy might strip headers. any fallback if header is gone?

maria: yes — ask for any client-side logs showing the response status and response body. Also ask them to grep for any header-like tokens in their app logs: common names are `x-request-id` or `x-redwood-req` or `x-rw-req-id`.

maria: If they can run curl (or we give them a copyable command), ask them to run with verbose trace so we can see header exchange even if proxy mutates things: 
```
curl -v -X POST 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  --data '{"input":"hello"}' \\n  --trace-ascii debug.trace \
  -o response.json
```
Tell them to attach `debug.trace` and `response.json`. Tell them to redact the token but keep the exact header names.

devon: if proxy terminates TLS (corporate mitm), TCP captures might still show host/paths. Ask for a lightweight pcap: 
```
sudo tcpdump -i any host api.redwood.example -w redwood_capture.pcap -s 0
```
Have them share the pcap (or a link). If they're uncomfortable, ask for the first 1MB of the pcap or a trimmed file.

karen-support: For Android/iOS SDKs, quick snippets to ask customer to log locally: 
- Node/Express example to print response headers: 
```js
fetch(url, opts).then(r => { console.log('status', r.status); r.headers.forEach((v,k)=>console.log(k+': '+v)); return r.json(); })
```
- Android (okhttp interceptor): 
```java
@Override public Response intercept(Chain chain) throws IOException { Response r = chain.proceed(chain.request()); Log.i("RW", "resp-headers: " + r.headers().toString()); return r; }
```
These logs often include the server-provided request id even if the browser/devtools view is missing it due to proxy.

sam: good. also what do we need to escalate to eng?

maria: Escalation bundle (minimal):
- customer account id / org id
- exact URL + path + timestamp (UTC)
- copy-as-curl or curl trace file (debug.trace)
- response.json (raw body) or screenshot of response headers/Network pane
- pcap if proxy suspected, otherwise HAR if available
- brief note on whether the client is behind any gateway/proxy, and whether auth passed (we only need redacted token)

maria: Add this sentence for non-technical customers: "If you can't run commands, please open Chrome DevTools -> Network -> reproduce -> right-click the failing request -> Save as HAR with content, and attach the HAR file."

devon: If there is absolutely no request id in any artifact, include the full response body and a timestamp so we can correlate in our backend logs by time and customer id. Also include the client IP if they can find it in their logs.

sam: I'll send that checklist. I'll also paste the curl and a short template they can copy. Thanks. :thumbsup:

karen-support: If they prefer, offer a short screenshare at a scheduled time and we can guide them through Copy as cURL / HAR — often faster for non-technical users.

devon: I can take the escalated bundle once they upload. ping me with the resulting filenames and I'll search our logs around the UTC timestamps.

sam: sent the checklist to the customer. closing thread unless they come back with files.
